blind.payload: Before writing, run a GO/NO-GO poll: for each memory line, mark GO (directly applies to this change request), NO-GO (contradicts it or is stale), or SILENT (irrelevant). Use only GO lines; the change request overrides memory. Then issue exactly one command in the format: ACTION: <verb + target>; CONSTRAINTS: <from GO lines>; COMMIT CRITERIA: <observable check proving done>; ABORT IF: <condition to stop and report>. If any core field is unknown, issue HOLD: <the one missing fact>.
blind.source_mechanism: Launch Commit Criteria with a Go/No-Go poll (rocketry and mission control): before launch, every console is polled GO/NO-GO. The launch command goes out only with written pass/fail criteria and abort rules, and any criterion that can't be checked puts the count on a HOLD instead of proceeding on a guess.

knowing.source_mechanism: Strand-template mismatch repair and ledger reconciliation: the approved-write journal is the reference strand. Any line that no longer matches its checksum gets restored before the next step runs.
Shared common operating picture: the executing unit sees the whole battlespace, not just a filtered slice, so it doesn't miss dependent lines that keyword top-8 retrieval leaves out.
Full-ledger audit instead of sampled vouchers: the checker checks the writes against the complete restored state, so it can catch collateral and missing changes.

knowing.payload: PROCEDURE before writing the instruction: (1) Restate the request's intent in one line. (2) List every affected key with its exact current value and required new value, as KEY: old -> new. (3) List dependent or related keys that must stay unchanged. (4) State the done-condition: the exact final value of every listed key. (5) If the request is ambiguous or a key is missing from the visible state, say so explicitly. Do not guess.
knowing.source_mechanism: Commander's intent plus an explicit end-state: the order lists every target key, its exact old and new value, and what must not change, so the worker and checker check against a closed list.

weighted.payload: Treat the retrieved memory lines as your prior and the instruction as a new measurement. Before writing: (1) Find the innovation, meaning what the instruction adds to or contradicts in memory. (2) Weight it: specific, explicit, recent claims override vague memory; vague claims do not. (3) Gate it: zero innovation means no writes; a contradiction means an update that cites the memory line it replaces. Writes contain only the correction. Summary: state the innovation and what changed.
weighted.source_mechanism: Kalman filter measurement update (innovation gating): treat memory as the prior state estimate and the instruction as a new measurement, compute the innovation (residual), weight it by relative confidence (Kalman gain), reject outliers, and write only the correction.
